draft.title: Returned soldiers
card: Many soldiers came home from the First World War with wounds, lost limbs or illness. Others had shell shock, a name used then for the mental and nervous harm caused by war.
Shell shock was not well understood at the time. Some men struggled for years to work and to live with their families.
Governments tried to help men return to civilian life. Soldier settlement schemes gave returned soldiers farms, often with loans to start up.
Many settlers failed. Some blocks were on poor land, too small or short of rain, and many men had little farming experience. Many left their farms in debt.
draft.remember: Returned soldiers needed help to rebuild their lives, and the farm schemes often failed because of poor land.

opts: The mental and nervous harm that war caused some soldiers
A wound caused by shrapnel from exploding shells
A medal given to soldiers who survived heavy shelling
A farming loan offered to soldiers after the war
a.why: Shell shock was the name used then for mental and nervous harm from war. It is not a physical wound, though the name might suggest one because of the word shell.
a.clue: Think about harm to the mind and nerves, not the body.

b.q: In 1921, Tom, a returned soldier and former clerk, is given a small farm in a dry district under a soldier settlement scheme. After five years he leaves it in debt. Which reason fits the card best?
opts: The land was poor and he had little farming experience
The scheme gave farms only to men who were not wounded
The government took the farm back because he had shell shock
The scheme gave him land but no loan to start up
b.why: The card says many blocks were on poor land and many men lacked farming experience, which fits a clerk on a dry block. The card does not say the schemes refused wounded men or took farms back for shell shock, and it says loans were often given.
b.clue: Look at the land and at Tom's past job.

a.best: The mental and nervous harm that war caused some soldiers

b.best: The land was poor and he had little farming experience

problems.detail: The clue 'Think about harm to the mind and nerves, not the body' gives the answer away. It echoes the right option's 'mental and nervous harm' and rules out the only plausible distractor (the shrapnel wound), so a student can answer without knowing the idea.

The remember line says the schemes often failed 'because of poor land' alone. The card gives several reasons: poor land, blocks too small, too little rain, and the men's lack of farming experience. It leaves out inexperience, which question b relies on, so it oversimplifies the card.

check.summary: The facts are sound and both questions have one clear right answer. However, the clue for question a gives the answer away, and the remember line reduces the reasons for settler failure to poor land only, leaving out inexperience, which question b tests.
